answer: The panel reads the opal for a name, the knoll for a number, the pigment for a date, then asks the farm to account for all three at once. An honest proof costs 234 POA; the farm pays the same per proof but needs 510 of them, which totals 119340 POA. This epoch the gate asks one thing only: Dressmaker wool coat mark sewn into the hem rail, and the receipt must read each wool coat is a season of logged stitching plus a signed master-tailor record. A real proof settles maker, moment and hand in one breath. Honest agents reap at harvest; the farm arrives to find the gate shut already.
